articles.title: Indian IT Stocks Just Crashed to a Three-Year Low. One Warning From Accenture Did It.
articles.excerpt: The Nifty IT index sank as much as 5.6 percent on June 19, with TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech falling 5-8 percent, after Accenture flagged cautious client spending and an AI-driven shift that threatens the sector's labour-heavy model.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru; the Nifty IT index sank to a three-year low on June 19

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
Mint
Barron's

articles.nri_angle: India's IT majors are the largest sponsors of H-1B visas and the biggest employers of diaspora technologists abroad, so a demand slowdown colliding with a tighter US visa regime and AI layoffs threatens the very job pipeline that carried many NRIs overseas — even as the sector's heavy weighting in the Nifty hits diaspora portfolios directly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Reliance Just Filed for the Jio IPO. It Could Be the Biggest Stock Debut in India's History.
articles.excerpt: At the Reliance AGM on June 19, Mukesh Ambani said Jio Platforms' draft prospectus was filed with SEBI — a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares targeting roughly $4 billion, on a business brokerages value near $180 billion.
articles.image_caption: Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani, who announced the Jio Platforms IPO filing at the AGM

sources.label: Reuters
The Hindu BusinessLine
The Wall Street Journal
Outlook Business

articles.nri_angle: The Jio IPO offers NRIs a rare large-cap, liquid way to own the infrastructure behind 500 million Indian internet users — investable through NRE/NRO portfolio accounts — and stands as a real-time referendum on whether the diaspora and the world still believe in India's digital growth story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Banks Want to Lend Dollars Out of GIFT City. The Target: $55 Billion in Diaspora Money.
articles.excerpt: Lenders are asking the RBI to route loans through their offshore GIFT City units to amplify a revived FCNR deposit scheme — a 2013-style bid to pull in diaspora dollars and steady a rupee just recovering toward 94.
articles.image_caption: The GIFT One tower at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, India offshore financial hub

sources.label: Reuters
Mint
Nomura research note

articles.nri_angle: New Delhi is openly competing for NRI savings: rising FCNR deposit rates, hedging subsidies and a proposed GIFT City lending mechanism could channel up to $55 billion in diaspora dollars into India, handing overseas Indians an outsized role in defending the rupee and earning more attractive, currency-risk-free returns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Quietly Rewrote Its Foreigner Registration Rules. NRI Families With Foreign-Passport Kids Need to Read the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: The Immigration and Foreigners (Amendment) Rules, 2026 — in force since June 1 — scrap the old 14-day grace period for long-stay registration, allow late filing only in 'emergent circumstances,' and impose a new 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later takes a foreign citizenship.
articles.image_caption: A Republic of India Emergency Certificate, an official government travel document; new 2026 rules tighten registration duties for foreign nationals in India
articles.nri_angle: India's new 2026 immigration rules scrap the 14-day registration grace period for long-staying foreigners and impose a 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later acquires foreign citizenship — changes that directly affect OCI holders, NRIs with foreign-national spouses, and diaspora families raising children across two passports.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Canada Want a Trade Deal Signed This Year. For Three Million Indians in Canada, the Reset Is Personal.
articles.excerpt: Meeting on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian — their fourth in under a year — Narendra Modi and Mark Carney pledged to conclude a long-stalled Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the G20, aiming to double bilateral trade to $50 billion and explicitly leaning on the diaspora as the bridge between the two countries.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney; the two leaders met on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian
articles.nri_angle: India and Canada set a G20 deadline to conclude a long-stalled trade deal and double bilateral trade to $50 billion — a reset that directly affects the roughly three million people of Indian origin in Canada through talent-mobility, student-exchange and services provisions, after a two-year freeze that hit the diaspora's people-to-people ties hardest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Told Banks to Pay NRIs Whatever It Takes. Deposit Rates Have Already Jumped to 7%.
articles.excerpt: In a move last used during the 2013 Taper Tantrum, the Reserve Bank has scrapped interest-rate ceilings on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits until September 30 and is absorbing banks' hedging costs — a direct bid for the diaspora's dollars that has pushed rates from around 3% to as high as 7.1%.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai; the central bank scrapped rate caps on NRI deposits on June 17
articles.nri_angle: The RBI has temporarily lifted rate caps on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits, pushing returns from ~3% to as high as 7.1% — a rare, time-limited chance for NRIs to earn high, low-risk returns on dollars or rupees parked in Indian banks, but only until September 30 and with tricky rules on breaking older deposits.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Court Just Lifted a $100,000 Wall in Front of Immigrant Doctors. Indian-American Physicians Are Calling It a Win for Patients.
articles.excerpt: The American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin has welcomed a federal ruling striking down the Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B fee, warning the charge would have gutted rural and safety-net hospitals where international medical graduates — a large share of them Indian-trained — keep the lights on.
articles.image_caption: A United States federal courthouse; a federal judge struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee this week
articles.nri_angle: A federal court struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee that Indian-American physician group AAPI says would have crippled rural and safety-net hospitals — where Indian-trained doctors (21% of US immigrant physicians) are essential — but with an appeal likely and other anti-H-1B bills moving, the relief for the diaspora's medical community may be temporary.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Oil Lifeline Through Hormuz Is Reopening. The Peace Holding It Open Just Wobbled.
articles.excerpt: Tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz again after the US-Iran ceasefire, and an Indian-flagged ship is finally sailing home. But Friday's signing ceremony in Switzerland was scrapped, Iran is threatening transit fees, and roughly half of India's crude still rides on a 60-day truce.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; tankers resumed transiting the Strait of Hormuz this week after the US-Iran ceasefire
articles.nri_angle: Roughly half of India's crude and a huge share of its trade ride through the Strait of Hormuz, where nearly half its overseas migrants and seafarers work — so the strait reopening means steadier Gulf jobs, cheaper goods and a calmer rupee, while the 60-day truce's fragility keeps diaspora-held energy and shipping stocks on edge.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Handing Its UAE Passport and Visa Counters to a New Operator on July 1. Millions of NRIs Need to Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: From July 1, Al Hind Tours and Travels takes over passport, visa, OCI and attestation services across the Emirates — replacing BLS International and SGIVS Global. For the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE, every consular errand is about to run through a different door.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport; renewals, OCI cards and attestations in the UAE move to a new service provider on July 1
articles.nri_angle: Every passport renewal, OCI application and attestation for the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the world's largest expatriate Indian community — moves to a new operator on July 1, so families should finish what they can before June 30 and trust only official Embassy channels for what comes next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Fuel Retailers Have Hit Their Borrowing Limit Absorbing Rs 1 Trillion in Losses to Keep Pump Prices Frozen
articles.excerpt: Oil secretary Neeraj Mittal says state-run IOC, BPCL and HPCL can barely borrow more after eating Rs 1 lakh crore of first-quarter losses to shield Indian consumers from the Iran war's oil shock. The freeze cannot hold forever — and the diaspora's families pay either way.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Oil fuel station; state retailers have absorbed about Rs 1 trillion in losses to keep pump prices frozen
articles.nri_angle: India has frozen pump prices through the oil shock by making state retailers borrow against Rs 1 trillion in losses — a cushion that keeps inflation and the relatives NRIs support protected for now, but whose eventual breaking point will hit household budgets, the rupee and diaspora-held energy stocks alike.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Hands Out Rs 2,400 Crore to First-Time Workers Today. It's a Bet That India's Jobs Problem Can Be Bought Down.
articles.excerpt: At Vigyan Bhawan on Friday, the Prime Minister disburses the first big tranche of the Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana — a Rs 99,446 crore scheme that pays young Indians to enter the formal economy and pays employers to hire them.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who disbursed Rs 2,400 crore under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on June 19
articles.nri_angle: India is spending Rs 99,446 crore to pull its young workforce into the formal economy — a bet that, if it works, means households less dependent on diaspora remittances and a stronger demographic case for every NRI weighing an investment back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Years of Delay, India's Biggest Stock Exchange Files to Go Public. The NSE IPO Could Be Worth $57 Billion.
articles.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives market — has finally filed draft IPO papers, setting up a $2.6 billion windfall for its investors and a landmark listing that lands just as India throws its equity markets open to NRIs.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, which filed draft papers for a landmark IPO
articles.nri_angle: India is listing the exchange at the heart of its markets just as it raises the limits on how much NRIs can own in Indian companies — a one-two move that courts the diaspora as a permanent class of domestic-market investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Rewrote the Rulebook for 4.5 Million OCI Holders. The Fine Print Forces a Hard Choice on Dual-Passport Families.
articles.excerpt: A sweeping overhaul moves Overseas Citizen of India casework fully online and promises 15-day approvals, but a mandatory passport-update rule with fines, colliding with new US disclosure demands, leaves diaspora families caught between two governments.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport and travel documents; India has overhauled the OCI program for its global diaspora
articles.nri_angle: OCI holders ARE the diaspora — 4.5 million of them — and this overhaul both speeds up their casework and, colliding with new US disclosure rules, forces dual-passport families into a long-deferred choice between an American and an Indian passport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai Has 40 Days of Drinking Water Left, and the Monsoon Is Running on Empty
articles.excerpt: The city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs sink to roughly 10 per cent of capacity, forcing water cuts on construction and industry while Maharashtra waits on a monsoon that may be the weakest in 11 years.
articles.image_caption: The Mumbai skyline; the city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs run low
articles.nri_angle: The huge Mumbai and Maharashtra diaspora has family weathering the cuts firsthand, while a weak monsoon stokes food inflation that quietly raises the real cost of the money NRIs send home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Arms Factories Just Hit a Record, and the Private Sector Is Finally Getting a Real Cut
articles.excerpt: Defence production touched an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY26 as exports surged past ₹38,000 crore — the clearest sign yet that India's bid to turn from the world's biggest arms importer into a maker and seller is gaining traction.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who announced India's record defence production for FY26
articles.nri_angle: A diaspora that has long watched India rank as the world's biggest arms importer now sees it building and exporting its own security, with the defence-tech boom drawing in exactly the high-skilled, globally networked talent the diaspora is full of.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Clawed Back From 97. Now the RBI's Own $110 Billion Bet Is What Stands Between It and a Real Rally.
articles.excerpt: A collapse in oil prices after the US-Iran deal pulled the currency to a six-week high near 94.3. But economists say the central bank's record short-dollar forward book will absorb the inflows before NRIs feel the gain.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, where policymakers have rolled out measures to attract dollar inflows
articles.nri_angle: The exchange rate decides what every remitted dollar is worth to family in India, and NRIs weighing FCNR and NRE deposits now face a rare window of high deposit rates and a still-cheap but recovering rupee.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Abroad Sent Home a Record $135 Billion. It Quietly Covered Nearly Half the Trade Deficit.
articles.excerpt: On the UN's International Day of Family Remittances, the numbers tell a story of a diaspora that has become India's most reliable line of external defence — and a center of gravity that has shifted from the Gulf to Silicon Valley.
articles.image_caption: Currency notes representing global money transfers
articles.nri_angle: Overseas Indians are the source of this record $135 billion lifeline, and the same US visa crackdown squeezing the diaspora directly threatens the high-skilled remittance pipeline India now leans on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: For the First Time, the Diaspora Unrolls Its Mats at the Lincoln Memorial for Yoga Day
articles.excerpt: The Indian Embassy chose one of America's most sacred civic spaces for the 12th International Day of Yoga, anchoring a global campaign built this year around 'Yoga for Healthy Aging.'
articles.image_caption: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., the venue for the Indian Embassy's International Day of Yoga 2026 celebration
articles.nri_angle: An ageing first generation of Indian Americans makes this year's 'Healthy Aging' theme deeply personal, while the Lincoln Memorial venue stakes the diaspora's claim to belonging at a tense moment in US-India ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.excerpt: A freeze on F-1 visa appointment slots and a 10-year-high 35% denial rate have stalled the Fall 2026 intake — prompting an emergency embassy outreach to students and a growing pivot toward the UK, Canada and India.
articles.image_caption: Students wait for F-1 student visa interviews during a special US Embassy visa workday.
